name: Advance to Chill Dog
summary: Advancing to Chill Dog clears the head-side arm around the neck from New York while the bottom player keeps the trapped arm isolated and the controlling knee hugged.
description: Advancing to Chill Dog clears the head-side arm around the neck from New York while the bottom player keeps the trapped arm isolated and the controlling knee hugged.
overview:
The bottom guard player begins in New York, facing a top player whose posture is controlled. This advances an existing rubber-guard arm trap; it does not move a turtle defender under a ride.

Keep the opposing hand on the mat and hug the knee before changing the head-side grip. Bring the knee toward the chest through hip movement so the neck-clearing motion does not twist the knee. Move the controlling arm around the head while keeping the leg and trapped arm connected.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs); [Eddie Bravo — Chill Dog / Invisible Collar clarification](https://www.10thplanetjj.com/forum/threads/17657-Chill-Dog-Invisible-Collar-Question).

Chill Dog can support a submission chain toward a separately established Carni shoulder lock or Gogoplata shin-under-chin enclosure. Preserve the arm isolation, then confirm the new shoulder or neck configuration before adding any finishing pressure.

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): What secures the arm before the head-side grip changes?
flashcards.answer: Keep the opponent's hand outside on the mat and hug your knee over that arm before changing the grip around the head.
flashcards.answer_line: Hand on mat; knee hugged over arm

plausible: Leave their forearm on your chest
Release knee hug to reach past head
trap: Wrist grip only, with your knee away

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): How do you make room to clear the head?
flashcards.answer: The hip angle brings the supported knee forward so the hand can clear the head without hauling the foot across a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Turn hip; bring knee toward chest

plausible: Stay flat; pull foot farther across
Send the knee away from your chest
trap: Lift ankle while keeping hips flat

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): Which arm moves around the head?
flashcards.answer: The head-side arm changes position around the head while the other arm retains the New York overhook and knee support.

plausible: Overhook arm, after letting knee go
Both arms, letting the high leg go
trap: Neither arm; move only the free leg

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): Where should the forearm resist forward pressure?
flashcards.answer: An inside forearm near the shoulder line keeps forward pressure from folding the frame onto your own wrist.

plausible: Outside shoulder, with wrist folded
Outside upper arm, with elbow wide

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): What keeps the isolated arm from returning inside?
flashcards.answer: Retain the arm wrap and knee hug as you consider the next control; a cleared head alone does not secure the elbow.
flashcards.answer_line: Overhook plus knee hug over that arm

plausible: Both hands pulling behind the head
Only the free foot on their hip
trap: High knee with the overhook released

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): Their elbow escapes as posture rises; what comes next?
flashcards.answer: Once the elbow and posture control are lost, recover knees and forearms between the bodies instead of chasing the high connection.
flashcards.answer_line: Open high leg; restore inside frames

plausible: Leave loose high leg behind the head
Chase their elbow with both hands

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): Which starting relationship supports this entry?
flashcards.answer: The performer is underneath in New York, controlling posture and one opposing arm before clearing the head-side connection.
flashcards.answer_line: Facing New York with one arm trapped

plausible: Mission Control; both elbows frame
Low closed guard; hands at chest
trap: High guard; wrist held, elbow inside

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): What changes from New York to Chill Dog?
flashcards.answer: The transition changes the arm position around the head while retaining the existing isolated arm and supported high leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Head-side arm clears; knee hug stays

plausible: Second leg closes behind their head
Trapped hand returns to the chest
trap: Knee hug opens; head grip stays

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): Your knee twists during neck clearing; what should stop?
flashcards.answer: Knee twisting means the foot is being pulled against a fixed joint; stop that traction and rebuild a comfortable hip angle.
flashcards.answer_line: Stop foot pull; reset your hip angle

plausible: Pull foot higher before turning hip
Fix the foot and straighten the knee
trap: Keep ankle tension as hips slide

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): Which connection should a first entry drill retain?
flashcards.answer: Rehearse clearing the head-side arm while the New York overhook and knee hug remain connected, without finishing pressure.
flashcards.answer_line: Overhook and knee hug stay connected

plausible: Head pull with their elbow inside
High foot grip with unsupported knee
trap: Knee hug alone; let the overhook go

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): What must change before a Gogoplata follow-up?
flashcards.answer: Chill Dog supplies a neck-cleared arm trap. A Gogoplata needs a separate shin-under-chin enclosure before it is a choke setup.
flashcards.answer_line: The shin must enter beneath the chin

plausible: The shin must rest across the jaw
Shin resting on the collarbone
trap: High calf across their upper back

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (bottom): What confirms the Chill Dog checkpoint?
flashcards.answer: Confirm both the cleared head-side arm and the retained overhook/knee hug; completing a hand movement alone is insufficient.
flashcards.answer_line: Head-side arm clear; arm trap intact

plausible: Head clear; their elbow back inside
Knee hugged; head-side arm unchanged
trap: Two high legs with the arm trap open

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (top): How should you use the free hand early?
flashcards.answer: Keep the available hand useful as an inside frame without letting the isolated elbow drift farther away from your ribs.

plausible: Reach over shoulder onto upper back
Flare the caught elbow for more room
trap: Post both hands outside their hips

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (top): Which movement signals the shift beyond New York?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player's grip change around your head while the knee hug stays connected is the neck-clearing cue.

plausible: Their pummel first lifts your wrist
Their ankles close behind your waist
trap: Their knee hug traps your arm on mat

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (top): Which leg movement would reinforce their high control?
flashcards.answer: An approaching second leg behind your head reinforces the existing high clinch; use an early frame and balanced base to deny it.
flashcards.answer_line: Free leg closes behind your head

plausible: Free knee returns between the bodies
High leg lowers toward your waist
trap: Free foot posts low beside their hip

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (top): When can the isolated elbow return toward your ribs?
flashcards.answer: Recover the elbow through available slack rather than pulling a captured shoulder against the high-leg connection.
flashcards.answer_line: High leg opens; shoulder can move

plausible: The free hand first touches the mat
Grip changes; knee hug stays tight

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (top): What should precede raising the head and chest?
flashcards.answer: Lift posture in stages after the head and isolated shoulder are free to move through the opened control.

plausible: Knees widen; head stays trapped
Arms push; shoulder remains caught
trap: Free leg drops; high leg still holds

flashcards.question: Advance to Chill Dog (top): Their high guard folds onto the neck; what should change?
flashcards.answer: When pressure folds the partner onto the neck, stop driving forward and unload so the high leg can be released safely.
flashcards.answer_line: Unload stack; let the high leg open

plausible: Drive forward with both knees wide
Lift their hips to shorten the loop
trap: Keep weight forward until leg drops
